newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia won't release all evidence to U.N. court.
newsitem.headline: Croatia won't release all evidence to U.N. court.

text.p: Croatia invoked national security on Tuesday and refused to supply all evidence sought for the trial of a Bosnian Croat general by the U.N. war crimes tribunal for former Yugoslavia.
The state news agency Hina quoted Foreign Minister Mate Granic as saying the government wanted to cooperate but would not set a precedent by releasing classified information.
"Croatia is willing to hand over to the court a part of documentation that does not interfere with vital national security issues," he said.
The tribunal, which sits in The Hague, has been seeking the evidence concerning General Tihomir Blaskic since the start of the year.
The court told Croatia it would summon Defence Minister Gojko Susak for an explanation if the evidence were not produced by August 18.

Blaskic, 36, is accused of involvement in the ethnic cleansing of Bosnian Moslems during the Moslem-Croat war in central Bosnia in 1993, when he commanded the Bosnian Croat militia. That force was armed by Croatia.

Political sources said the wanted documents included Blaskic's notes to the Croatian Defence Ministry, its records on arms supplies to Bosnian Croats and orders he received from the head of the separatist Bosnian Croat entity.
Croatia has been under strong international pressure to comply with the tribunal and the United States has blocked two loans because it was not satisfied with Zagreb's record to date.
Granic said there were indications the pressure to comply with the Blaskic subpoena could be reduced if other indicted Bosnian Croats went to The Hague.
Croatia has extradited only one indicted Croat war criminal to the tribunal. Blaskic surrendered voluntarily in the spring of 1996.
